tasks.short: Review policy terms and loss evidence to assess insurance coverage.

steps.what: Retrieve the policy version and loss record from the insurance administration system {OTHER}.
Read policy documents and endorsements to identify relevant terms.

loop.input: The applicable policy wording, endorsements and loss record.
loop.output: Relevant clauses with quotations, page references and unresolved terms.
loop.check: Verify quotations against the source and document version; a representative checks clause relevance.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; missing or conflicting wording goes to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clause relevance depends on varied wording and endorsements; fixed keyword rules miss material context.

steps.what: Request missing loss details through {EMAIL}.
Compare loss evidence with coverage, exclusions and conditions; write a provisional assessment.

loop.input: Reviewed clauses, loss facts, evidence and approved interpretation guidance.
loop.output: A provisional coverage assessment separating facts, interpretations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Every material statement links to evidence or a clause; a representative checks omissions and reasoning.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguity or unsupported conclusions require manual assessment.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applying narrative exclusions to disputed facts requires contextual interpretation beyond fixed coverage rules.

steps.what: Approve the coverage determination within delegated authority or escalate disputed interpretation.
Record and send the approved coverage explanation through {HELPDESK}.

tasks.design: An integration retrieves the applicable policy and loss records from {OTHER}; a bounded reading loop produces cited clauses and a provisional assessment in {HELPDESK}. A claims handler approves the determination, after which templates record and send the approved explanation through {HELPDESK} and {EMAIL}. Evidence requests have their own approval before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy versions, endorsements and loss evidence were scattered, while interpretation could not safely be reduced to lookup rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster integration development and bounded document reading reduce retrieval and drafting effort. Policy interpretation still needs accountable review.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting endorsements, disputed facts and consequential coverage decisions remain expensive to assess.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when literal wording misses the material facts, explain uncertainty and take responsibility for the determination.

ambition.what: A pre-submission evidence check for customers with incomplete loss notifications.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more time resolving missing evidence and explaining difficult cases. They can prioritise evidence collection; binding coverage rights remain with the delegated claims role.

reach.task: Prepare clear coverage notices from approved determinations.
reach.learn: Cited drafting, accessible explanations and the distinction between an assessment and an approved decision.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-based question answering with handover is available; this does not establish reliable insurance coverage interpretation.
Retrieval, cited drafting and human coverage approval are a proposed design, without an insurance-specific case in the digest.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its exceptions.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to an insurance service team, rather than every customer service department.
Today's steps and time shares are estimates for a mid-size European company.
Representatives assess routine cases; a delegated claims role approves consequential determinations.
The high automation prior overstates substitution here because policy interpretation and approval retain substantial human time.
Build ranges cover one policy family and one connected insurance administration system.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules determine any employee consultation requirements.
unknowns: Which policy versions and endorsements are accessible in machine-readable form?
Which coverage decisions can representatives legally and operationally approve?
Are medical or other special-category data present?
Which access approvals and employee consultation processes apply?
research_questions: How often do reviewed clause suggestions omit a material exclusion or endorsement?
Which evidence checks can be expressed as reliable fixed rules?
Does assisted assessment improve explanation quality without increasing incorrect coverage conclusions?
new_work: Review clause selection and provisional assessments.
Maintain policy versions, evidence checklists and approved interpretations.
Investigate conflicting documents and unsupported citations.
Check access controls, retention and integration failures.

tasks.short: Offer relevant additional products or services during customer interactions.

steps.what: Review the customer's current services and contact preferences in {CRM}.
Decide whether an additional offer fits the customer and current interaction.
Ask about needs and listen during a customer call.
Explain a suitable offer, its price and limitations; address customer questions.
Record needs, interest and agreed follow-up in {CRM}.

loop.input: Brief representative notes and the selected offer.
loop.output: Structured needs, expressed interest and agreed follow-up, with unknown fields left blank.
loop.check: Validate catalogue identifiers; the representative confirms interest and follow-up before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; incomplete notes use a structured form.
loop.why_not_simpler: Brief narrative notes vary; a bounded extraction avoids retyping them into several fields.

steps.what: Create a follow-up lead and assign it to a sales representative in {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure {CRM} to show current services, contact preferences and rule-eligible offers beside the customer record. The representative chooses whether to raise an offer and conducts the conversation; a bounded loop converts their notes into a reviewed interest record. Existing {CRM} routing then assigns the agreed follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service history and offer conditions took time to assemble, while conversational judgement offered little scope for fixed automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration can assemble account context, and small extraction loops can reduce repeated note entry.
tasks.still_hard: Timing, trust, suitability and responding to hesitation remain human work. Catalogue and eligibility data must stay current.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when the customer needs help rather than an offer, and explain trade-offs without pressure.

ambition.what: Customers whose existing service duplicates or exceeds their stated needs.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time searching and logging, with most conversation time retained. They gain a clearer basis for choosing a helpful offer; pricing and contract authority do not expand.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Coach representatives on offer timing and customer outcomes.
reach.learn: Review conversation examples, distinguish expressed interest from consent, and assess suitability beyond conversion.

evidence.claim: A customer-facing shopping assistant exists, but this does not demonstrate equivalent performance in human service conversations.
A documented support-assistant study found productivity gains, especially for novices; it did not establish sales conversion gains.
Account briefs, eligibility filters and lead routing can use deterministic configuration.

assumptions: This is occasional additional-service solicitation during support work, not a primary sales role.
Today's steps and time shares are estimates; live conversation dominates this task.
The baseline uses representative notes and does not introduce call recording or employee scoring.
Known eligibility, contact preferences and duplicate-service checks can be expressed as rules.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules govern any consultation required by later recording or monitoring changes.
unknowns: Are service holdings, prices and eligibility rules available together?
Which contact preferences and marketing permissions must be enforced?
Can representatives suggest lower-cost alternatives as well as additional services?
Which access and consultation approvals apply?
research_questions: Does the account brief reduce preparation time without increasing unsuitable offers?
Would a structured form be faster than note extraction for the team's actual notes?
Which customer outcome measures reveal pressure or poor suitability?
new_work: Confirm extracted interest and follow-up details.
Maintain catalogue eligibility, pricing and routing rules.
Resolve duplicate leads and stale account data.
Review examples of unsuitable offers for coaching.

tasks.short: Match disputed goods to order records and prepare the appropriate return credit document.

steps.what: Read the merchandise dispute and attachments in {HELPDESK}.

loop.output: Claimed order references, disputed items, quantities and reasons, each linked to its source.
loop.check: Match references to account records; a representative confirms ambiguous items and quantities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; unresolved identifiers go to manual intake.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customers describe goods and disputes in varied prose and attachment layouts.

steps.what: Retrieve the customer order, original invoice and shipment record from {ERP}.
Inspect disputed goods against the shipment record and record their condition.
Reconcile disputed items, quantities and prices in a return worksheet.
Approve the return value and any policy exception.
Prepare and post the credit note linked to the original invoice in {ERP}.
Send the credit note and update the customer case through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A bounded intake loop in {HELPDESK} identifies disputed lines, while deterministic integration matches them to orders and invoices in {ERP} and inspections in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Fixed checks calculate the proposed credit and detect duplicate or excessive returns; people inspect goods and approve return exceptions and value. After approval, {ERP} generates the credit note and {HELPDESK} sends the matching notice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer descriptions, warehouse findings and financial records lacked shared identifiers, so staff reconciled them manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing return functions can handle posting and document generation; inexpensive integration and bounded extraction connect the remaining gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, disputed quantities, partial returns and responsibility for damage still require evidence and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve contested condition or responsibility fairly, and recognise when the standard return policy produces an unreasonable outcome.

ambition.what: A customer-visible return status covering inspection, authorisation and credit issuance.

tasks.altitude: The representative handles disputed evidence and customer explanations instead of copying financial lines. They can resolve reconciliation exceptions within existing limits; credit approval rights stay delegated.

reach.task: Reconcile return credits against outstanding customer balances.
reach.learn: Credit-note allocation, duplicate-credit controls and the difference between a credit and a cash refund.

evidence.claim: Document-based order capture can validate customer, stock and price data and route exceptions before posting.
Order import and stock synchronisation already exist, supporting deterministic record exchange.
Return reconciliation and approved credit-note generation are proposed extensions; the digest provides no direct returns case.

assumptions: This task applies to a company handling physical goods.
A credit note is the usual return document here; the required document depends on the transaction and national rules.
The worksheet represents manual reconciliation between departments, not a replacement for financial records in {ERP}.
Time shares describe the full handoff chain, including warehouse and finance work.
Build ranges cover one order flow, one warehouse connection and established return rules.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national employee consultation requirements must be checked where working practices change.
unknowns: Does {ERP} support linked partial credits and prevent cumulative over-crediting?
Who approves routine returns and which exceptions need supervisor approval?
Are inspection results linked to individual order lines?
Which tax treatments, document formats and access approvals apply?
research_questions: What share of disputes can match directly to an original invoice line?
Which exceptions arise from missing identifiers rather than genuine judgement?
Can existing {ERP} return configuration remove the need for custom posting code?
new_work: Review uncertain item extraction and unmatched lines.
Maintain return rules and approval limits.
Investigate duplicate credits, failed postings and reconciliation differences.
Keep warehouse inspection identifiers aligned with financial order lines.

tasks.short: Gather complaint evidence, examine possible causes and assess whether the complaint is valid.

steps.what: Hear the customer's complaint and clarify the disputed outcome during a call.
Retrieve billing, service events and previous contacts across {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}.
Request missing readings, dates or supporting documents through {EMAIL}.
Compare charges, dates and usage in a worksheet; flag unexplained differences.
Read contextual evidence and service policies to identify plausible causes.

loop.input: Reconciled records, complaint narrative, service policies and relevant context evidence.
loop.output: An evidence-linked list of plausible causes, contradictions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require sources for factual claims; the representative checks alternatives and rejects unsupported causal conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; insufficient or contradictory evidence returns to manual investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative complaints and context vary; fixed checks cannot explain every service event or competing account.

steps.what: Assess complaint validity and decide whether specialist investigation is needed.
Record findings and route unresolved causes to the responsible service team.

tasks.design: Deterministic integrations assemble a dated evidence pack from {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}, then calculate billing and usage differences. A bounded reading loop compares the pack with policies in {DOCS} and drafts possible explanations with sources and uncertainties. The representative assesses validity, while {HELPDESK} records the approved findings and routes unresolved questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was split across teams and records, and contextual explanations required manual reading after basic reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster integration development makes evidence assembly cheaper, while bounded drafting can organise varied narratives without deciding validity.
tasks.still_hard: Missing readings, conflicting accounts and separating correlation from cause remain difficult. Weather alone cannot establish why an individual bill changed.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh conflicting evidence, hear what the customer disputes and recognise when a plausible explanation is insufficient.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of recurring billing causes for service operations investigation.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more time testing explanations and resolving disputed facts. They can prioritise investigation referrals within agreed limits; refund and policy-exception authority require separate delegation.

reach.task: Reproduce a suspected billing or account-display defect from a complaint.
reach.learn: Write reproducible steps, preserve event timelines and distinguish a data defect from a policy disagreement.

evidence.claim: Customer-service tools can answer questions and access order information through integrations.
A documented support-assistant study found higher issues resolved per hour; this does not establish accurate complaint-validity decisions.
Deterministic reconciliation plus reviewed explanation drafting is a proposed design; causal validity still needs human assessment.

assumptions: The illustrated company has billing and service-event records; weather evidence is relevant only for some complaints.
Today's steps and time shares are estimates, with substantial retrieval effort but persistent judgement work.
The worksheet ties records together where existing screens lack a cross-record comparison.
The design supports assessment and referral; it does not automatically reject complaints or issue refunds.
No new call recording, emotion recognition or employee performance scoring is introduced.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; access and any employee consultation follow applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which records share reliable customer, account and event identifiers?
Are tariffs, readings and service events complete and historically versioned?
Which contextual evidence is available and licensed for use?
What assessment, escalation and remedy authority does each role hold?
Which data access and employee consultation processes apply?
research_questions: Which recurring complaint causes can be tested with deterministic checks?
Does the evidence pack reduce investigation time while preserving contradictory evidence?
How often do drafted explanations suggest a cause unsupported by the record?
new_work: Review proposed causes and evidence gaps.
Maintain tariff rules, evidence checklists and routing.
Resolve missing identifiers and failed evidence retrieval.
Sample assessments for unsupported explanations and missed alternatives.

role.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult conversations, evidence disputes and explanation quality. Better preparation supports broader investigation work, while financial and coverage decision rights remain explicitly delegated.
reach: Prepare clear, approved correspondence with a correspondence clerk.
Reconcile return credits with a credit clerk.
Turn recurring complaints into reproducible investigations with a computer user support specialist.
Support customer-outcome coaching with a first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers.
skills_to_grow: Read source-linked evidence and challenge unsupported conclusions.
Understand billing, return and coverage rules within delegated authority.
Conduct needs-led conversations and explain uncertainty clearly.
Write reproducible referrals and recognise recurring service failures.
Review structured records and identify integration exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: A service resolution specialist who combines customer conversations with evidence analysis, runs a recurring complaint-cause review and proposes targeted service improvements.
